title: Clip candidates and chapter boundaries for a long chat podcast
what_it_does: From the audio and the word transcript (and speakers.json when it exists) proposes the best 15-45 s clip candidates for Shorts/Reels and chapter boundaries. Each clip carries a transparent score from measured signals (laughter-like bursts in the audio plus laugh words in the transcript, loudness, quick speaker turns, reaction lines and a standalone opening sentence) minus penalties (needs earlier context, starts mid-sentence, long silence, unsure words in the first 3 s). Writes moments.json and moments.md (top 8 clips with the transcript excerpt and reasons, chapter list) for the person to choose from.
when_to_use: After transcribe-local on a long conversational recording (about 10 minutes and more, two or more voices), when the person wants Shorts/Reels or YouTube chapters and has not named the moments. Not for a single-speaker lesson with no reactions (the text and laughter signals have little to find) and never a substitute for the person listening: it cannot hear whether a joke is funny.
notes: Pure JS maths on a 16 kHz mono decode; deterministic; zero dependencies. A 28-minute episode takes about 6 s. Pitch is not measured. Laughter detection precision/recall on synthetic audio is in the README; on real speech it has no ground truth yet.
